newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan seeks changes in Jinnah film script.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seeks changes in Jinnah film script.

text.p: Pakistan has asked the producers of a film on the nation's founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah to change the script or forfeit official sponsorship, a government official said on Wednesday.

Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's adviser on information and culture Mushahid Hussain told a news conference the government would not release 60 million rupees ($1.5 million) allocated to the project unless revisions were made.
"After reviewing the script, my recommendation is that it should be revised," Hussain said, adding that the changes should be made in consultation with the director, Akbar Ahmed.
Sharif asked Hussain to review the script after some local newspapers attacked the film for casting Christopher Lee, best known for portraying Count Dracula, in the title role.
The newspapers also criticised what they said was a fanciful script unworthy of official sponsorship.

"Unless some parts of the script are revamped the government of Pakistan will not release the funds," Hussain said, but added that filming could go ahead without government money if the producers did not want to change the script.
"If they make the film on their own, they are most welcome. The only issue is that since they have asked for money from the government of Pakistan, our involvement is there."
The Jinnah tribute is being produced in Pakistan's golden jubilee year, a half-century after the nation was carved from British India amid the blood-stained upheaval of Partition.
State-run Pakistan television, banks and individual Pakistanis are among other investors in the project, which has a modest budget of five million sterling ($8 million).
